root.header: "Ballad of Booker T.," by Langston Hughes, June 1, 1941 BALLAD OF BOOKER T. by Langston Hughes

interpretation.note: Booker T. earnestly believed that hard work (plus more as we see later) would support the cause of African Americans.

root.interpretation: Booker T. Was a practical man. He said, Till the soil And learn from the land.

interpretation.note: The 'fate' of African-Americans can be found where they currently live, not far away in another country or even state.

root.interpretation: Let down your bucket Where you are. Your fate is here And not afar.

interpretation.note: A community must be educated, kind, and hard-working for any true change to emerge. Nobody can push for change without someone to help them eat.

root.interpretation: To help yourself And your fellow man, Train your head, Your heart, and your hand. For smartness alone's Surely not meet— If you haven't at the same time Got something to eat.

interpretation.note: Booker T. created a university that taught both book and hands-on skills, something that couldn't have been done before harnessing community.

root.interpretation:
Thus at Tuskegee
He built a school With book-learning there And the workman's tool. He started out In a simple way— For yesterday Was not today.

interpretation.note: While some compromises had to be made, for the time and place, Booker T. did the best he could.

root.interpretation: Sometimes he had Compromise in his talk— For a man must crawl Before he can walk— And in Alabama in '85 A joker was lucky To be alive.

interpretation.note: While the spectre of racism loomed over him, Booket T. did help in creating the dream of full equality in his time.

root.interpretation: But Booker T. Was nobody's fool: You may carve a dream With an humble tool. The tallest tower Can tumble down If it be not rooted In solid ground.

interpretation.note: Again, Booker T. wanted to encourage community skills and learning in his time, believing in a more prosperous, equal future.

root.interpretation: So, being a far-seeing Practical man, He said, Train your head, Your heart, and your hand. Your fate is here And not afar, So let down your bucket Where you are.
root.footer: LANGSTON HUGHES Final Draft, Hollow Hills Farm, Monterey, California, June 1, 1941.
